translation: Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition. For every choice of types P, D, E, R, every record t of type S3 P D E R, and every r in R, let Q be the set of p in P for which some o in t.c1(p) satisfies t.c3(o) = r. For each p in P, let U(p) be the union of t.c2(o) over all o in t.c1(p), not just those with t.c3(o) = r. Suppose there exists a function S from Q to Q and there exists a p in Q such that U(p) and U(S(p)) are disjoint. Disjointness is required only for that p, and S(p) is not required to differ from p. Then there exists an o in D that belongs to t.c1(q) for some q in P and satisfies both t.c3(o) = r and t.c4(t.c3(o)) ∉ t.c2(o). The conclusion does not require q to be p or S(p).

judgement.summary: The hypothesis matches Definition 3.1, and the conclusion gives a dataset that can arise, has inference content r, and exhibits a falsification. This is Lemma 3.5; the same witness establishes Lemma 3.3 without the inference-content requirement.
